question: What is the main goal of rehabilitation nursing compared to regular hospital care?

options.B: Strictly monitoring vital signs every hour

explanation: While acute hospital care focuses on curing the disease, rehab is all about helping patients rebuild their strength and independence so they can live life to the fullest. You've got this! [learn more](GNS123_U6_T2#GNS123_U6_T2_h1)

question: When should the rehabilitation journey ideally start for a patient who has suffered a major injury?

options.A: When the patient asks to start walking
options.B: Only after the patient is discharged home
options.C: As soon as the patient is medically stable

explanation: Rehab starts early—right after the patient is medically stable—to prevent stiffness and get a head start on recovery. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T2#GNS123_U6_T2_h1)

question: Which member of the healthcare team is a medical doctor who specializes in physical medicine and rehab?
explanation: A physiatrist is a doctor who leads the medical side of physical medicine and rehabilitation. Great job keeping terms straight! [learn more](GNS123_U6_T2#GNS123_U6_T2_h2)

question: A patient is having a hard time buttoning their shirt and holding a toothbrush after a stroke. Who should step in to help with these daily tasks?
explanation: Occupational therapists are experts at helping patients regain fine motor skills for daily activities like dressing, eating, and brushing teeth. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T2#GNS123_U6_T2_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of the initial evaluation phase in rehabilitation?

options.A: Discharging the patient permanently to their home
options.B: Identifying baseline functional deficits and recovery potential
options.D: Stopping all medications to test natural healing

explanation: Before planning treatment, the team checks what the patient can and cannot do yet so they can build a personalized recovery plan. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T2#GNS123_U6_T2_h3)

question: Why is recovery in rehabilitation often described as non-linear or up-and-down?

options.A: Therapists change goals randomly every single day
options.B: Insurance companies dictate how many phases a patient must skip
options.C: Medical staff rarely document patient improvements
options.D: Patients often experience setbacks that require adjusting the care plan

explanation: Healing isn't a straight line! Good days and bad days happen, and nurses adjust care plans to match how the patient is feeling. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T2#GNS123_U6_T2_h3)

question: What is the main reason nurses use functional assessment tools in rehab?

options.A: To calculate the exact date a patient will leave the hospital
options.B: To diagnose the exact strain of bacteria causing an infection
options.C: To determine the financial cost of hospital stay
options.D: To measure a patient's ability to perform activities of daily living

explanation: Assessment scales give nurses an easy way to track how well a patient is managing basic self-care tasks over time. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T2#GNS123_U6_T2_h4)

question: Why is it so important to set rehabilitation goals together with the patient?

options.A: Patients usually know more about pharmacology than doctors do
options.B: Hospital policies legally forbid nurses from writing goals alone
options.C: Goals matter more and motivate the patient when they reflect personal values
options.D: Collaborative goals take less time to write out in charts

explanation: When patients help choose their goals, they feel heard and stay much more motivated to work hard during therapy! [learn more](GNS123_U6_T2#GNS123_U6_T2_h4)

question: Which nursing action helps prevent joint stiffness (contractures) in a patient on bed rest?

options.A: Restricting fluid intake to reduce swelling
options.B: Keeping the bed locked in a flat position all day
options.D: Applying ice packs to every major joint

explanation: Moving joints gently through their full range keeps muscles and tendons flexible and stops them from tightening up permanently. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T2#GNS123_U6_T2_h5)

question: A patient is on strict bed rest. What is the most effective nursing action to prevent bedsores (pressure injuries)?

options.A: Applying thick layers of adhesive bandages over the heels
options.B: Massaging reddened bony prominences vigorously with alcohol
options.C: Repositioning the patient on a regular two-hour schedule
options.D: Turning the patient only once during the night shift

explanation: Turning patients every two hours takes the pressure off bony areas, keeping the skin healthy and intact. Brilliant nursing care! [learn more](GNS123_U6_T2#GNS123_U6_T2_h5)

question: When should discharge planning ideally start for a patient admitted to a rehab unit?

options.D: When the patient asks to go home

explanation: Starting discharge planning on day one ensures family training and home changes are sorted out smoothly without last-minute panic. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T2#GNS123_U6_T2_h6)

question: What is a major risk if a patient goes home without proper family training and home preparation?

options.A: Immediate complete recovery of motor function
options.C: Decreased need for community follow-up care

explanation: Without preparation, families may struggle at home, leading to setbacks that unfortunately send the patient right back to the hospital. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T2#GNS123_U6_T2_h6)
